title: Anatomy of an eyeris Object
text: preprocessing .asc EyeLink files eyeris, returned objects class eyeris, contain key components used throughout package’s backend. key components : file: original file path source .asc file block: block number time_orig: raw tracker time (ms) time_secs: normalized tracker time, starting 0 (seconds) eye_x: eye position x-coordinate eye_y: eye position y-coordinate eye: eye (Left Right) recorded data sourced hz: tracker sampling rate (hz) type: whether source data recorded using diameter area method pupil_raw: raw recorded pupil source data arbitrary units (.u.) ’ll notice preprocessing step run, new column added pupil_raw column; new columns follow structure subsequent step appended previous columns name (.e., pupil_raw_{previous steps}_{current_step}). illustrate: pupil_raw -> pupil_raw_deblink -> pupil_raw_deblink_detransient -> … events: list data frames containing trial event messages timestamps blinks: list data frames containing start/stop/durations blinks info: EyeLink EDF header data parsed data frame latest: internal tracker used assessing steps run far confounds: list data frames containing confounding variables preprocessing step (see: 📊 summarize_confounds()) params: detailed list steps run parameters passed step epoch_{name}: list data frames given epoched timeseries 💡 Note: vignette describes structure eyeris object returned main preprocessing pipeline. Understanding components help interpret results, debug issues, extend pipeline research needs. Furthermore, binocular data left right component eyeris object, contain components main eyeris object. also phantom raw_binocular_object component eyeris object, contains raw binocular data used internally perform binocular correlation analysis plotting. title: Chunked eyerisdb Database Export for Large Datasets
text: easiest way export entire database eyeris_db_to_chunked_files(): Using eyeris_db_to_chunked_files() function defaults, : - Process 1 million rows time (.e., default chunk size) - Create files 500MB (.e., default max file size) - Export data types found database - Save files bids_dir/derivatives/eyerisdb_export/-proj/

title: Chunked eyerisdb Database Export for Large Datasets
text: specialized analysis, can process chunks custom functions:
code: # Connect to database directly con <- eyeris_db_connect("/path/to/bids", "large-project")  # Define custom analysis function for pupil data analyze_chunk <- function(chunk) {   # Calculate summary statistics for this chunk   stats <- data.frame(     n_rows = nrow(chunk),     subjects = length(unique(chunk$subject_id)),     mean_eye_x = mean(chunk$eye_x, na.rm = TRUE),     mean_eye_y = mean(chunk$eye_y, na.rm = TRUE),      mean_pupil_raw = mean(chunk$pupil_raw, na.rm = TRUE),     mean_pupil_processed = mean(chunk$pupil_raw_deblink_detransient_interpolate_lpfilt_z, na.rm = TRUE),     missing_pupil_pct = sum(is.na(chunk$pupil_raw)) / nrow(chunk) * 100,     hz_modes = paste(unique(chunk$hz), collapse = ",")   )      # Save chunk summary (append to growing file)   write.csv(stats, "chunk_summaries.csv", append = file.exists("chunk_summaries.csv"))      return(TRUE)  # Indicate success }  # Hypothetical example: process large timeseries dataset in chunks result <- process_chunked_query(   con = con,   query = "     SELECT subject_id, session_id, time_secs, eye_x, eye_y,             pupil_raw, pupil_raw_deblink_detransient_interpolate_lpfilt_z, hz     FROM timeseries_01_enc_clamp_run01      WHERE pupil_raw > 0 AND eye_x IS NOT NULL      ORDER BY time_secs   ",   chunk_size = 100000,   process_chunk = analyze_chunk )  eyeris_db_disconnect(con)

text: load EyeLink pupillometry data, need .asc file converted original .edf file using official EyeLink edf2asc command-line utility provided SR Research. Expected Data Format: .asc file standard EyeLink ASCII output file containing: Sample data timestamps, gaze coordinates (x, y), pupil size Event messages (e.g., MSG lines trial markers, stimulus onsets) Recording metadata (sample rate, pupil measurement type, etc.) Example Code Loading Custom Data: Important Notes: File Path: Replace "/path///data/participant_01.asc" actual path .asc file. Block Handling: Use block = "auto" (default) automatically detect multiple recording segments within file. recommended use cases. See ?eyeris::load_asc options. Binocular Data: binocular recordings, can specify handle : Data Quality: Ensure data recorded without online filtering applied EyeLink Host PC. eyeris pipeline expects raw, unfiltered data. See Caveats section details critical requirement.
code: # Point to your own .asc file my_data_path <- "/path/to/your/data/participant_01.asc"  # Load the data file my_data <- eyeris::glassbox(my_data_path) # Average both eyes (default) my_data <- eyeris::glassbox(   my_data_path,   load_asc = list(binocular_mode = "average") )  # Use only left eye my_data <- eyeris::glassbox(   my_data_path,   load_asc = list(binocular_mode = "left") )  # Use only right eye my_data <- eyeris::glassbox(   my_data_path,   load_asc = list(binocular_mode = "right") )  # Process both eyes independently my_data <- eyeris::glassbox(   my_data_path,   load_asc = list(binocular_mode = "both") )

code: ***WARNING: SOMETHING OUTRAGEOUS IS HAPPENING WITH YOUR PUPIL DATA!***   The median absolute deviation (MAD) of your pupil speed is 0.  This indicates a potential setup / hardware issue which has likely propogated   into your pupil recording. Most often, this is due to online filtering being   applied directly to your pupil data via the EyeLink Host PC.   WE DO NOT RECOMMEND USING ANY ONLINE AUTO FILTERING DURING YOUR DATA RECORDING.   ***ADDITIONAL INFO*** The default setting for communicating with the EyeLink  machine is to have filtering enabled on either live-streamed data or saved data   in EDF files.  We do not want these filters because:  (1) it is unclear how the EyeLink machine is specifying their low-pass filter,  and (2) it conflicts with an assumption here in `eyeris::detransient()` to use   one-step difference to compute a threshold for detecting large jumps in pupil   data (suggesting blinking or other artifacts).   ***GENERAL TIP***  You should aim to have your data as raw as possible so you can 'cook' it fresh!   ***WHAT TO DO NEXT***  If you would like to continue preprocessing your current pupil data file,  you should consider skipping the `eyeris::detransient()` step of the pipeline   altogether. Advanced users might consider additional testing by manually   passing in different `mad_thresh` override values into `eyeris::detransient()`   and then carefully assessing the consequences of any given override value on   the pupil data; however, this step is not recommended for most users.   PLEASE CONTINUE AT YOUR OWN RISK.

code: winsorize_pupil <- function(x, prev_op, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99) {   vec <- x[[prev_op]]   q <- quantile(vec, probs = c(lower, upper), na.rm = TRUE)   vec[vec < q[1]] <- q[1]   vec[vec > q[2]] <- q[2]   vec }

code: #' Winsorize pupil values #' #' Applies winsorization to extreme pupil values within each block. #' #' @param eyeris An `eyeris` object created by [load_asc()]. #' @param lower Lower quantile threshold. Default is 0.01. #' @param upper Upper quantile threshold. Default is 0.99. #' @param call_info A list of call information and parameters. If not provided, #'   it will be generated from the function call. #' #' @return Updated `eyeris` object with new winsorized pupil column. winsorize <- function(eyeris, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99, call_info = NULL) {   # create call_info if not provided   call_info <- if (is.null(call_info)) {     list(       call_stack = match.call(),       parameters = list(lower = lower, upper = upper)     )   } else {     call_info   }    # handle binocular objects   if (is_binocular_object(eyeris)) {     # process left and right eyes independently     left_result <- eyeris$left |>       pipeline_handler(         winsorize_pupil,         "winsorize",         lower = lower,         upper = upper,         call_info = call_info       )          right_result <- eyeris$right |>       pipeline_handler(         winsorize_pupil,         "winsorize",         lower = lower,         upper = upper,         call_info = call_info       )          # return combined structure     list_out <- list(       left = left_result,       right = right_result,       original_file = eyeris$original_file,       raw_binocular_object = eyeris$raw_binocular_object     )      class(list_out) <- "eyeris"      return(list_out)   } else {     # regular eyeris object, process normally     eyeris |>       pipeline_handler(         winsorize_pupil,         "winsorize",         lower = lower,         upper = upper,         call_info = call_info       )   } }

previous_headings: Introduction > Why Use Databases Instead of CSV Files?
title: Working with eyeris Databases: A Complete Guide
text: 1. Scalability Performance Massive datasets: processing hundreds thousands subjects, CSV files can become unwieldy. single database file can efficiently store data thousands participants. Faster queries: Instead reading multiple CSV files filtering R, databases can filter aggregate data storage level, dramatically reducing memory usage processing time. Concurrent access: Multiple researchers can query database simultaneously without file locking issues. 2. Cloud Computing Advantages Reduced /O costs: cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), reading many small CSV files incurs significant /O costs. single database file reduces costs dramatically. Bandwidth efficiency: Transferring one database file much faster syncing thousands CSV files. Storage optimization: Databases compress data efficiently individual CSV files. 3. Data Integrity Management Schema validation: Built-data type validation prevents corruption. Metadata storage: Databases automatically track creation timestamps, data types, relationships. 4. Analysis Efficiency SQL queries: Leverage power SQL complex filtering, aggregation, joins. Memory efficiency: Load data need instead entire datasets. Cross-platform compatibility: DuckDB databases work across R, Python, analysis platforms.

code: # first connect to your eyeris project database con <- eyeris_db_connect("~/processed_study_data", "attention_study_db")  # write your custom SQL query custom_query <- "   SELECT subject_id, session_id, task_name,           AVG(pupil_raw_deblink_detransient_interpolate_lpfilt_z) as mean_pupil,          COUNT(*) as n_samples   FROM timeseries_001_01_attention_task_run01_eyeL    WHERE pupil_clean IS NOT NULL   GROUP BY subject_id, session_id, task_name "  results <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, custom_query) print(results)  # a complex cross-table query complex_query <- "   SELECT e.subject_id,          e.matched_event,          e.text_unique,          AVG(t.pupil_raw_deblink_detransient_interpolate_lpfilt_z) as mean_pupil_in_epoch,          c.blink_rate_hz   FROM epochs_001_01_attention_task_run01_stimulus_response_eyeL e   JOIN timeseries_001_01_attention_task_run01_eyeL t      ON e.subject_id = t.subject_id      AND t.time_orig BETWEEN e.epoch_start AND e.epoch_end   JOIN run_confounds_001_01_attention_task_run01_eyeL c     ON e.subject_id = c.subject_id   GROUP BY e.subject_id, e.matched_event, e.text_unique, c.blink_rate_hz "  complex_results <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, complex_query) print(complex_results)

what: Example 2: Quality Control and Confounds Analysis
title: Working with eyeris Databases: A Complete Guide
text: eyeris reports proportion missing (NA) pupil samples prop_missing column (raw count, n_missing) two levels: per recording block (run_confounds) per epoched event/trial (confounds_events). eyeris apply fixed missing-data exclusion cutoff . Instead, columns exposed can define exclusion thresholds whichever level (block, epoch, trial) appropriate design.
code: # extract confounds data for quality control confounds_data <- eyeris_db_collect(   "~/processed_study_data",   data_types = c("run_confounds", "confounds_events") )  # block-level QC: identify subjects with poor data quality # (all thresholds below are illustrative -- choose values appropriate for your # study; nothing here is enforced by eyeris) quality_control <- confounds_data$run_confounds %>%   group_by(subject_id, session_id) %>%   summarise(     mean_blink_rate = mean(blink_rate_hz, na.rm = TRUE),     mean_prop_missing = mean(prop_missing, na.rm = TRUE),     mean_prop_invalid = mean(prop_invalid, na.rm = TRUE),     mean_gaze_variance = mean(gaze_x_var_px, na.rm = TRUE),     .groups = 'drop'   ) %>%   mutate(     high_blink_rate = mean_blink_rate > 0.5,  # user-defined thresholds     high_missing_data = mean_prop_missing > 0.5,     high_invalid_data = mean_prop_invalid > 0.3,     high_gaze_variance = mean_gaze_variance > 10000,     exclude_subject = high_blink_rate | high_missing_data |       high_invalid_data | high_gaze_variance   )  # then view the subjects you have flagged for exclusion exclude_list <- quality_control %>%   filter(exclude_subject) %>%   select(subject_id, session_id, exclude_subject)  print(exclude_list)  # trial-level QC: flag individual epochs/trials to drop using your own # missing-data threshold (e.g., here, > 50% missing on the deblinked signal) trial_exclusions <- confounds_data$confounds_events %>%   filter(grepl("deblink", step)) %>%   mutate(exclude_trial = prop_missing > 0.5) %>%  # user-defined threshold   select(     subject_id, session_id, run_number, epoch_label,     matched_event, n_samples, n_missing, prop_missing, exclude_trial   )  print(trial_exclusions)

Create separate databases for different experiments bidsify(data, db_path = "experiment_1_attention") bidsify(data, db_path = "experiment_2_memory")   # 4. always disconnect from databases con <- eyeris_db_connect("~/data", "study_db") # ... do your work ... # then disconnect ... eyeris_db_disconnect(con)  # or use on.exit for automatic cleanup process_data <- function() {   con <- eyeris_db_connect("~/data", "study_db")   on.exit(eyeris_db_disconnect(con))      # ... your analysis code here ...      results <- eyeris_db_collect("~/data", "study_db")   return(results) }

code: # 1. Use database-only workflow to minimize I/O costs process_cloud_data <- function(subject_list, input_bucket, output_bucket) {   for (subject in subject_list) {     # ... for demo purposes only -- download raw data ...     download_from_cloud(subject, input_bucket)          # ... process and add to database (no CSV files) ...     eyeris_data <- glassbox(local_file) %>%       epoch(...)          bidsify(       eyeris_data,       bids_dir = "local_processing",       participant_id = subject,       csv_enabled = FALSE,  # skip CSV for cloud efficiency       db_enabled = TRUE,       db_path = "cloud_study_db"     )          # clean up local files     unlink(local_file)   }      # upload final database back to your cloud   upload_to_cloud("cloud_study_db.eyerisdb", output_bucket) }  # 2. use database for distributed analysis analyze_cloud_data <- function() {   # download only the database file   download_from_cloud("cloud_study_db.eyerisdb")      # extract only the data you need   analysis_data <- eyeris_db_collect(     "local_processing",     data_types = c("epochs", "confounds_summary"),     subjects = target_subjects   )      # run analysis on extracted subset   results <- run_statistical_analysis(analysis_data)      return(results) }

what: Converting Existing CSV Data to Database
title: Working with eyeris Databases: A Complete Guide
code: # if you have existing eyeris-derived CSV files and want to migrate to a database migrate_csv_to_database <- function(bids_dir, db_path) {   # ... find all CSV files ...   csv_files <- list.files(bids_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$",                           recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)      # ... connect to an eyeris database ...   con <- eyeris_db_connect(bids_dir, db_path)   on.exit(eyeris_db_disconnect(con))      for (csv_file in csv_files) {     cat("Processing:", basename(csv_file), "\n")          # parse filename to extract metadata     # ... (which of course depends on your CSV naming convention) ...     filename_parts <- parse_bids_filename(basename(csv_file))          # ... read CSV data ...     csv_data <- read.csv(csv_file)          # ... then write to the eyeris project database ...     write_eyeris_data_to_db(       data = csv_data,       con = con,       data_type = filename_parts$data_type,       sub = filename_parts$subject,       ses = filename_parts$session,       task = filename_parts$task,       # ... other parameters     )   }      cat("Migration complete!\n") }

what: Exporting Database Data Back to CSV
title: Working with eyeris Databases: A Complete Guide
code: # export specific data back to CSV format (if needed) export_database_subset <- function(bids_dir, db_path, output_dir) {      # ... extract data from the eyeris project database ...   data <- eyeris_db_collect(bids_dir, db_path,                               subjects = c("001", "002"),                              data_types = c("timeseries", "events"))      # ... create an output directory ...   dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)      # ... then export each data type ...   for (data_type in names(data)) {     filename <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(data_type, "_subset.csv"))     write.csv(data[[data_type]], filename, row.names = FALSE)     cat("Exported:", filename, "\n")   } }

what: Example C: Epoch with Subtractive Baselining
title: Extracting Data Epochs and Exporting Pupil Data
text: Use 1-second window "DELAY_STOP" baseline apply epoch data. example, ’re extracting 1-second epochs following "PROBE_START" event applying subtractive baseline correction. baseline computed 1-second window corresponding "DELAY_STOP" event. words, means pupil trace normalized subtracting average pupil size pre-probe delay period (.e., baseline period).
code: eye_1c <- eye |>   epoch(     events = "PROBE_START_{trial}",     limits = c(0, 1),     label = "probeEpochs",     calc_baseline = TRUE,     apply_baseline = TRUE,     baseline_type = "sub",     baseline_events = "DELAY_STOP_*",     baseline_period = c(-1, 0)   )

what: The one concept to know: block is run
title: Preprocessing Multiple Runs Stored in Separate Files
text: eyeris, input knob called block (block argument load_asc()), output BIDS entity called run (run-<index> token derivative filenames). map one--one: block N input  →  run-0N output set block number file, setting run number. “Block” eyeris/experiment-design terminology; “run” BIDS acquisition entity. (block entity BIDS – separately-acquired repetition task run.) , workflow , set run number via load_asc(block = ...) need pass run_num bidsify().

title: Preprocessing Multiple Runs Stored in Separate Files
text: Suppose participant AB01 completed three runs associative-memory task, saved file: piece : load_asc = list(block = ) sets run number file. iteration = 1 file becomes block_1 → run-01, = 2 → run-02, . Passing single numeric block also forces entire file one run, exactly want one file = one run (Sanity check ). epoch() extracts trials. TST_trial-{trial}_{item}_{associate} matches trial event parses trial, item, associate columns epoched data frame. bidsify() writes run’s derivatives. participant_id, session_num, task_name every iteration, three runs land subject/session tree, distinguished run-<index>. ℹ️ run_num bidsify() call? bidsify() inherits run number eyeris object – .e., block set load_asc(). Setting bidsify() redundant. (run_num exists relabel single-run object – e.g. force lone file saved run-03 – silently ignored objects already contain multiple blocks.)
code: library(eyeris)  dl <- path.expand("~/Downloads") asc_files <- file.path(dl, c(   "sub-AB01_t1_2024-01-15_10h00.00.000.asc",   "sub-AB01_t2_2024-01-15_10h30.00.000.asc",   "sub-AB01_t3_2024-01-15_11h00.00.000.asc" )) stopifnot(all(file.exists(asc_files)))  output_dir <- path.expand("~/Documents/eyeris")  for (i in seq_along(asc_files)) {   glassbox(asc_files[i], load_asc = list(block = i), verbose = TRUE) |>     epoch(       events = "TST_trial-{trial}_{item}_{associate}",       limits = c(0, 0.1),       label  = "trialEpochs"     ) |>     bidsify(       bids_dir       = output_dir,       participant_id = "AB01",       session_num    = "01",       task_name      = "assocmem",       save_raw       = TRUE,       html_report    = TRUE,       report_seed    = 0     ) }

what: The equivalent: label the run in bidsify() instead
title: Preprocessing Multiple Runs Stored in Separate Files
text: Setting run number input load_asc(block = ) form recommend, one. single-run file already loads one block default, can leave load_asc untouched instead label file output bidsify(run_num = ) – exactly “relabel single-run object” use run_num note . loop writes run-01, run-02, run-03 derivatives one : two changes first loop : (1) glassbox() longer receives load_asc = list(block = ), file loads default single block; (2) bidsify() now takes run_num = , relabels block run-01, run-02, etc. Everything else – every output file – . ⚠️ two forms equivalent genuinely single-run files. run_num relabels file resolves one block; file happens contain multiple embedded recording segments, run_num ignored (bidsify() emit warning verbose = TRUE) runs numbered embedded blocks instead. load_asc(block = ) also forces whole file single run, doubles guard accidentally-multi-segment files. prefer run_num form, worth running sanity check confirm file really one run.

text: common, important question: “runs 1–3 run 2 never collected? run 3 get saved run 2?” – eyeris never renumbers runs. run number written disk exactly number assign via block =. global counter re-sequences runs across files. one thing watch get number . loop , block = uses loop position, equals true run number files really runs 1, 2, 3, … order none missing. run 2 never collected files runs 1 3, seq_along() hand file #2 (run-3 file) index 2 mislabel run-02. fix drive run number true run identity, loop position. Two robust options: Option – explicit vector run numbers, paired files: Option B – parse run number filename. run encoded _t1_, _t2_, _t3_, small regex recovers (naturally handles gaps, since missing run simply file): either approach, run 3 saved run-03 gap preserved. ℹ️ Gaps valid BIDS. BIDS specification require run indices consecutive – dataset run-01 run-03 run-02 perfectly valid, faithfully records actually collected. need “compress” run numbers fill gap.
code: asc_files <- file.path(dl, c(   "sub-AB01_t1_2024-01-15_10h00.00.000.asc", # run 1   "sub-AB01_t3_2024-01-15_11h00.00.000.asc"  # run 3 (run 2 not collected) )) run_nums <- c(1, 3) # the TRUE run numbers, in the same order as `asc_files`  for (i in seq_along(asc_files)) {   glassbox(asc_files[i], load_asc = list(block = run_nums[i]), verbose = TRUE) |>     epoch(       events = "TST_trial-{trial}_{item}_{associate}",       limits = c(0, 0.1),       label  = "trialEpochs"     ) |>     bidsify(       bids_dir       = output_dir,       participant_id = "AB01",       session_num    = "01",       task_name      = "assocmem",       save_raw       = TRUE,       html_report    = TRUE,       report_seed    = 0     ) } for (f in asc_files) {   run_n <- as.integer(sub(".*_t(\\d+)_.*", "\\1", basename(f)))    glassbox(f, load_asc = list(block = run_n), verbose = TRUE) |>     epoch(       events = "TST_trial-{trial}_{item}_{associate}",       limits = c(0, 0.1),       label  = "trialEpochs"     ) |>     bidsify(       bids_dir       = output_dir,       participant_id = "AB01",       session_num    = "01",       task_name      = "assocmem",       save_raw       = TRUE,       html_report    = TRUE,       report_seed    = 0     ) }

what: Sanity check: confirm one run per file
title: Preprocessing Multiple Runs Stored in Separate Files
text: EyeLink .asc files sometimes contain one recording segment (instance, tracker stopped restarted recalibration drift correct). eyeris auto-detects multiple segments file, treats file multi-block – case run_num ignored runs numbered embedded block numbers instead block = . Passing single numeric block () forces whole file one run, want one-file-per-run data. can confirm file resolves exactly one run checking length $timeseries: length(eye$timeseries) comes back greater 1 file expected single run, file split multiple blocks; forcing block = <run number> (single numeric, ) collapses back one run.

title: Flexible, Extensible, & Reproducible Pupillometry Preprocessing
text: Despite decades pupillometry research, many established packages workflows unfortunately lack design principles based (F)indability ()ccessbility ()nteroperability (R)eusability (FAIR) principles. eyeris, hand follows thoughtful design philosophy results intuitive, modular, performant, extensible pupillometry data preprocessing framework. Much design principles heavily inspired Nipype. eyeris also provides highly opinionated pipeline tonic phasic pupillometry preprocessing (inspired fMRIPrep). opinions product many hours discussions core members signal processing experts Stanford Memory Lab (Shawn Schwartz, Mingjian , Haopei Yang, Alice Xue, Anthony Wagner). eyeris also introduces BIDS-like structure organizing derivative (preprocessed) pupillometry data, well intuitive workflow inspecting preprocessed pupillometry epochs within beautiful, interactive HTML report files (see demonstration ⬇)! package also includes gaze heatmaps show distribution eye coordinates across entire screen area, helping assess data quality participant attention patterns. heatmaps automatically generated BIDS reports can also created manually.

text: eyeris object class eyeris derived load_asc() save_all Logical flag indicating whether epochs saved subset . Defaults TRUE epochs_list List epochs saved. Defaults NULL bids_dir Base bids_directory. Defaults NULL participant_id BIDS subject ID. Defaults NULL session_num BIDS session ID. Defaults NULL task_name BIDS task ID. Defaults NULL run_num BIDS run ID. Optional override run number one block data present given .asc file. allows manually specify run number (e.g., "03") instead using default block number .asc files (1). especially useful single .asc file single run task want BIDSified derivatives labeled correctly. However, files multiple recording blocks embedded within .asc file, parameter ignored blocks automatically numbered runs (block 1 = run-01, block 2 = run-02, etc.) order appeared/recorded. Defaults NULL (override) save_raw Logical flag indicating whether save_raw pupil data addition epoched data. Defaults TRUE html_report Logical flag indicating whether save eyeris preprocessing summary report HTML file. Defaults TRUE report_seed Random seed plots appear report Defaults 0. See plot() detailed description report_epoch_grouping_var_col String name grouping column use epoch--epoch diagnostic plots interactive rendered HTML report. Column name must exist (.e., custom grouping variable name set within metadata template epoch() call). Defaults "matched_event", epoched data frames valid column name. disable epoch-level diagnostic plots, set NULL verbose flag indicate whether print detailed logging messages. Defaults TRUE. Set FALSE suppress messages current processing step run silently csv_enabled Logical flag indicating whether write CSV output files. Defaults TRUE. Set FALSE disable CSV file generation, useful large-scale cloud compute environments using database storage db_enabled Logical flag indicating whether write data DuckDB database. Defaults FALSE. TRUE, creates connects database centralized data storage querying db_path Database filename path. Defaults "eyeris-proj.eyerisdb". just filename, database created derivatives/ directory. full path provided, used specified parallel_processing Logical flag manually enable parallel database processing. TRUE, uses temporary databases avoid concurrency issues. Defaults FALSE (auto-detect based environment variables) merge_epochs (Deprecated) parameter deprecated ignored. epochs now saved separate files following BIDS conventions. parameter removed future version merge_runs (Deprecated) parameter deprecated ignored. runs now saved separate files following BIDS conventions. parameter removed future version pdf_report (Deprecated) Use html_report = TRUE instead

Users prefer using glassbox() rather invoking function directly unless specific reason customize pipeline manually. Computed properties: pupil_speed: Compute speed pupil approximating derivative x (pupil) respect y (time) using finite differences. Let \(x = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)\) \(y = (y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n)\) two numeric vectors \(n \ge 2\); , finite differences computed : $$\delta_i = \frac{x_{+1} - x_i}{y_{+1} - y_i},      \quad = 1, 2, \dots, n-1.$$ produces output vector \(p = (p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n)\) defined : first element: $$p_1 = |\delta_1|,$$ last element: $$p_n = |\delta_{n-1}|,$$ intermediate elements (\(= 2, 3, \dots, n-1\)): $$p_i = \max\{|\delta_{-1}|,\,|\delta_i|\}.$$ median_speed: median computed pupil_speed: $$median\_speed = median(p)$$ mad_val: median absolute deviation (MAD) pupil_speed median: $$mad\_val = median(|p - median\_speed|)$$ mad_thresh: threshold computed median speed MAD, using constant multiplier \(n\) (default value: 16): $$mad\_thresh = median\_speed + (n \times mad\_val)$$

title: Downsample pupil time series with anti-aliasing filtering — downsample
text: Downsampling reduces sampling frequency decimating data points. function automatically designs anti-aliasing filter using lpfilt() function carefully chosen parameters: ws (stopband frequency) = Fs_new / 2 (Nyquist freq new sampling rate) wp (passband frequency) = ws - max(5, Fs_nq * 0.2) error raised wp < 4 prevent loss pupillary responses resulting time points : 0, 1/X, 2/X, 3/X, ..., etc. X new sampling frequency. input contains gaps longer interpolation limit (see interpolate()'s max_gap_ms) left NA, gaps temporarily filled anti-aliasing filter can run masked back NA. can slightly bias valid samples immediately adjacent gap toward interpolated values, warning emitted case. bias concern, consider disabling step (glassbox(downsample = FALSE)).

title: eyeris: Flexible, Extensible, & Reproducible Pupillometry Preprocessing — eyeris-package
text: Pupillometry offers non-invasive window mind used extensively psychophysiological readout arousal signals linked cognitive processes like attention, stress, emotional states [Clewett et al. (2020) doi:10.1038/s41467-020-17851-9 ; Kret & Sjak-Shie (2018) doi:10.3758/s13428-018-1075-y ; Strauch (2024) doi:10.1016/j.tins.2024.06.002 ]. Yet, despite decades pupillometry research, many established packages workflows date lack design patterns based Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, Reusability (FAIR) principles [see Wilkinson et al. (2016) doi:10.1038/sdata.2016.18 ]. 'eyeris' provides modular, performant, extensible preprocessing framework pupillometry data BIDS-like organization interactive output reports [Esteban et al. (2019) doi:10.1038/s41592-018-0235-4 ; Gorgolewski et al. (2016) doi:10.1038/sdata.2016.44 ]. Development supported, part, Stanford Wu Tsai Human Performance Alliance, Stanford Ric Weiland Graduate Fellowship, Stanford Center Mind, Brain, Computation Technology, NIH National Institute Aging Grants (R01-AG065255, R01-AG079345), NSF GRFP (DGE-2146755), McKnight Brain Research Foundation Clinical Translational Research Scholarship Cognitive Aging Age-Related Memory Loss, American Brain Foundation, American Academy Neurology.

title: Extract and aggregate eyeris data across subjects from database — eyeris_db_collect
text: bids_dir Path BIDS directory containing database db_path Database name (defaults "-project", becomes "-project.eyerisdb") subjects Vector subject IDs include. NULL (default), includes subjects data_types Vector data types extract. NULL (default), extracts available types. Valid types: "blinks", "events", "timeseries", "epochs", "epoch_summary", "run_confounds", "confounds_events", "confounds_summary" sessions Vector session IDs include. NULL (default), includes sessions tasks Vector task names include. NULL (default), includes tasks epoch_labels Vector epoch labels include. NULL (default), includes epochs. applies epoch-related data types eye_suffixes Vector eye suffixes include. NULL (default), includes eyes. Typically c("eye-L", "eye-R") binocular data verbose Logical. Whether print progress messages (default TRUE)

what: Export eyeris database to chunked files — eyeris_db_to_chunked_files
title: Export eyeris database to chunked files — eyeris_db_to_chunked_files
text: High-level wrapper function export large eyeris databases chunked CSV Parquet files data type. Uses chunked processing handle large datasets without memory issues.

title: Export eyeris database to chunked files — eyeris_db_to_chunked_files
code: eyeris_db_to_chunked_files(   bids_dir,   db_path = "my-project",   output_dir = NULL,   chunk_size = 1e+06,   file_format = "csv",   data_types = NULL,   subjects = NULL,   max_file_size_mb = 50,   group_by_epoch_label = TRUE,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Export eyeris database to chunked files — eyeris_db_to_chunked_files
text: bids_dir Path BIDS directory containing database db_path Database name (defaults "-project", becomes "-project.eyerisdb") output_dir Directory save output files (defaults bids_dir/derivatives/eyerisdb_export) chunk_size Number rows process per chunk (default: 1000000) file_format Output format: "csv" "parquet" (default: "csv") data_types Vector data types export. NULL (default), exports available subjects Vector subject IDs include. NULL (default), includes subjects max_file_size_mb Maximum file size MB per output file (default: 50). exceeded, automatically creates numbered files (e.g., data_01--03.csv, data_02--03.csv) group_by_epoch_label TRUE (default), processes epoch-related data types separately epoch label reduce memory footprint produce label-specific files. FALSE, epochs different labels merged single large files (recommended). verbose Whether print progress messages (default: TRUE)

what: Split eyeris database into N parquet files by data type — eyeris_db_to_parquet
title: Split eyeris database into N parquet files by data type — eyeris_db_to_parquet
text: Utility function takes eyerisdb DuckDB database splits N reasonably sized parquet files easy management GitHub, downloading, distribution. Data first grouped table type (timeseries, epochs, events, etc.) since different columnar structures, group split specified number files. Files organized folders matching database name easy identification.

title: Split eyeris database into N parquet files by data type — eyeris_db_to_parquet
code: eyeris_db_to_parquet(   bids_dir,   db_path = "my-project",   n_files_per_type = 1,   output_dir = NULL,   max_file_size = 512,   data_types = NULL,   verbose = TRUE,   include_metadata = TRUE,   epoch_labels = NULL,   group_by_epoch_label = TRUE )

title: Split eyeris database into N parquet files by data type — eyeris_db_to_parquet
text: bids_dir Path BIDS directory containing database db_path Database name (defaults "-project", becomes "-project.eyerisdb") n_files_per_type Number parquet files create per data type (default: 1) output_dir Directory save parquet files (defaults bids_dir/derivatives/parquet) max_file_size Maximum file size MB per parquet file (default: 512) Used constraint n_files_per_type create files larger data_types Vector data types include. NULL (default), includes available. Valid types: "timeseries", "epochs", "epoch_summary", "events", "blinks", "confounds_*" verbose Whether print progress messages (default: TRUE) include_metadata Whether include eyeris metadata columns output (default: TRUE) epoch_labels Optional character vector epoch labels include (e.g., "prepostprobe"). applies epoch-related data types. NULL, includes labels. group_by_epoch_label TRUE, processes epoch-related data types separately epoch label reduce memory footprint produce label-specific parquet files (default: TRUE).

Steps marked (default: ) run automatically; steps marked (default: ) skipped unless explicitly enable . preprocessing steps can turned passing <step> = FALSE (except load_asc, always runs file .asc path). Steps accept parameters can customized passing <step> = list(...) values want override (example, deblink = list(extend = 40)). Load data (load_asc, default: ) – Reads parses EyeLink .asc file eyeris object, automatically splitting recording blocks , binocular recordings, handling eye separately. See load_asc(). step skipped pre-loaded eyeris object passed file (see file parameter). Remove blinks (deblink, default: ) – Replaces missing data around blinks NAs, extending gap 50 ms either side rapid dips spikes surround blink removed . See deblink(). Remove transient artifacts (detransient, default: ) – Rejects pupil samples change faster physiologically plausible, using speed-based median absolute deviation (MAD) threshold. See detransient(). Interpolate missing samples (interpolate, default: ) – Fills NA gaps left deblink detransient steps using linear interpolation, producing continuous, gap-free time series. See interpolate(). Smooth signal (lpfilt, default: ) – Applies low-pass filter (default 4 Hz passband) remove high-frequency noise preserving slower pupil dynamics interest. See lpfilt(). Downsample (downsample, default: ) – Optionally lowers sampling rate using anti-aliasing filter, preserves temporal dynamics signal. combined bin. See downsample(). Bin (bin, default: ) – Optionally lowers sampling rate averaging samples within equal-width time bins. combined downsample. See bin(). Detrend (detrend, default: ) – Optionally fits linear model pupil ~ time returns residuals (along fitted slope intercept) remove slow linear drift. Use care – see detrend() appropriate. Z-score (zscore, default: ) – Rescales pupil time series mean 0 standard deviation 1, making values comparable across participants recordings. See zscore(). preprocessing, glassbox() calls summarize_confounds() compute per-step confound metrics (e.g., missingness gaze statistics) store $confounds. Crucially, step adds new column time series rather overwriting previous one, every intermediate stage preserved inside returned eyeris object. makes pipeline "glass box": can inspect, plot, compare data transformation (example, plot(output, steps = c(1, 5))).

title: Load pupillometry data from a non-EyeLink eye tracker — load_generic

code: # first, define your custom data preprocessing function winsorize_pupil <- function(x, prev_op, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99) {   vec <- x[[prev_op]]   q <- quantile(vec, probs = c(lower, upper), na.rm = TRUE)   vec[vec < q[1]] <- q[1]   vec[vec > q[2]] <- q[2]   vec }  # second, construct your `pipeline_handler` method wrapper winsorize <- function(eyeris, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99, call_info = NULL) {   # create call_info if not provided   call_info <- if (is.null(call_info)) {     list(       call_stack = match.call(),       parameters = list(lower = lower, upper = upper)     )   } else {     call_info   }    # handle binocular objects   if (eyeris:::is_binocular_object(eyeris)) {     # process left and right eyes independently     left_result <- eyeris$left |>       pipeline_handler(         winsorize_pupil,         "winsorize",         lower = lower,         upper = upper,         call_info = call_info       )      right_result <- eyeris$right |>       pipeline_handler(         winsorize_pupil,         "winsorize",         lower = lower,         upper = upper,         call_info = call_info     )      # return combined structure     list_out <- list(       left = left_result,       right = right_result,       original_file = eyeris$original_file,       raw_binocular_object = eyeris$raw_binocular_object     )      class(list_out) <- "eyeris"      return(list_out)   } else {     # regular eyeris object, process normally     eyeris |>       pipeline_handler(         winsorize_pupil,         "winsorize",         lower = lower,         upper = upper,         call_info = call_info       )   } }  # and voilà, you can now connect your custom extension # directly into your custom `eyeris` pipeline definition! custom_eye <- system.file("extdata", "memory.asc", package = "eyeris") |>   eyeris::load_asc(block = "auto") |>   eyeris::deblink(extend = 50) |>   winsorize()  plot(custom_eye, seed = 1) #> ℹ [2026-07-18 21:24:52] [INFO] Plotting block 1 with sampling rate 1000 Hz from #> possible blocks: 1

title: eyeris (development version)
text: BREAKING (#295): interpolate() now enforces maximum gap duration linear interpolation via new max_gap_ms parameter. Gaps consecutive missing (NA) samples longer max_gap_ms now left NA rather interpolated . default 250 ms follows recommendation Kret & Sjak-Shie (2018), advise interpolating across long gaps linear interpolation unlikely reflect true underlying pupil signal. Previously (eyeris ≤ 3.2.0), gaps interpolated regardless duration. change default behavior may affect downstream results; eyeris now prints console notice (per glassbox() run) limit effect. restore previous behavior interpolating across gaps, set interpolate = list(max_gap_ms = Inf) glassbox() (max_gap_ms = Inf calling interpolate() directly). threshold can also customized, e.g., glassbox(interpolate = list(max_gap_ms = 100)). limit specified milliseconds internally converted number samples using recording’s sampling rate, behaves consistently across sampling frequencies, @shawntz #295. ENH (#295): downstream glassbox() steps operate missing data — low-pass filtering (lpfilt()), downsampling (downsample()), binning (bin()), detrending (detrend()) — now work around gaps interpolate(max_gap_ms) intentionally leaves NA. filter/resample/fit available data (filling temporarily needed) restore gaps NA, long-gap NAs preserved final preprocessed output instead causing steps skipped. interpolation run upstream, filter/resample steps still raise usual “interpolate first” error, @shawntz #295. ENH (#295): lpfilt() downsample() now emit warning filter gaps longer max_gap_ms (left NA interpolate()). low-pass/anti-aliasing filter run missing data, gaps temporarily filled masked back NA; filter can therefore slightly bias valid pupil samples immediately adjacent gap toward (near-linear) interpolated values — analogous edge artifacts seen start/end filtered recording, repeated every long gap. warning lets decide whether disable filtering /downsampling (lpfilt = FALSE /downsample = FALSE) avoid introducing systematic bias, cost retaining high-frequency content. console warning fires per glassbox() run, information recorded “Data Quality Notes” section HTML preprocessing report captured part data provenance, @shawntz #295.

title: eyeris (development version)
text: NF (#299): Added load_generic(), tracker-agnostic data loader non-EyeLink eye trackers. now, load_asc() (SR Research EyeLink .asc files) implemented loader, prevented researchers using eye trackers running data eyeris. load_generic() accepts three standardized data frames — pupil (raw samples: timestamp + pupil size, optionally gaze eye_x/eye_y), events (timestamp + message text), blinks (blink start/end intervals) — plus optional fourth gaze data frame less common case gaze exported separately pupil size (joined onto pupil timestamp). assembled exact eyeris S3 object load_asc() produces, making result drop-input glassbox(), epoch(), bidsify(), plotting methods. Column names configurable via mapping argument; sampling rate inferred timestamps supplied; timestamps may provided milliseconds (default) seconds (time_unit = "s"); block/eye/pupil_type/screen-dimension metadata mirror load_asc(). Native readers specific tracker formats can now layered top function incrementally, @shawntz #299. NF: glassbox() now accepts pre-loaded eyeris object (e.g., load_generic()), automatically skipping file-loading step running remaining pipeline object directly. makes load_generic(...) |> glassbox() work expected, also means already-loaded load_asc() object piped glassbox() now processes correctly instead raising error. ENH (#300): Added hardware-quirk guardrail detects non-uniform sampling intervals input timeseries. Different eye trackers behave differently pupil data missing: EyeLink zero-fills, hardware silently drops samples, leaving gaps otherwise evenly spaced time vector. downstream pipeline steps (e.g., detransient(), lpfilt(), downsample()) assume fixed sampling rate, gaps can silently distort results. new internal check_uniform_sampling_intervals() helper infers expected inter-sample interval data (robust dropped samples sub-millisecond timestamp rounding), checks recording segment independently legitimate -block gaps flagged, emits informative warning estimating number dropped samples irregular intervals detected. also cross-checks data-derived interval device’s reported sampling rate catch systematic dropout (e.g., every Nth sample missing), leaves uniform coarser grid gap detection alone see. check wired load_asc() quirk surfaced early, preprocessing begins, @shawntz #308.
